summary: Pin-state reconciliation lag after shadow-replay during regional traffic surge
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Carousel Labs) reported that after a regional traffic surge and a subsequent shadow-replay test, some sessions that had been explicitly model-pinned to rw-g1-large-v1 became unpinned or routed to the fallback variant for a short window (~30-90s). This surfaced as mixed model outputs for existing user sessions and a spike in request latency and 5xxs for the customer

Impact:
- A subset of active sessions (10-15% of customer traffic during the surge) received responses from the fallback variant instead of the pinned model.
- Visible quality regressions for customer end users and a billing spike due to extra fallback invocations.
- Customer-facing: degraded UX on personalization flows; reported by Carousel Labs CS on 2026-03-14 09:12 UTC.

Environment:
- prod - us-east (dedicated pool for Carousel Labs)
- Model: rw-g1-large-v1 (pinned via tenant policy)
- Canary/shadow: recent shadow-replay job for rw-g1-large-v2 that was running simultaneous to surge

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer has long-lived session tokens pinned to rw-g1-large-v1.
2) Traffic spike (external) causes autoscaler prewarm and scheduler churn.
3) Shadow-replay job for the v2 candidate runs on overlapping edge shard; replay load overlaps active tenant traffic.
4) Orchestrator snapshot merge during scheduler rebalance shows delayed pin-state commit for some session cohorts.
5) Requests for those sessions are routed via fallback path until pin-state fully reconciles (~0.5-1.5 minutes).

Observed behavior:
- Pin-state TTLs reported stale on several orchestrator nodes (metrics: pin_reconcile_latency spiked from baseline ~200ms to >4s).
- Edge retry queues for the affected shard showed bursts and some retry-induced header mutation (x-tenant-pin) on proxied requests.
- Canary shadow jobs emitted replay traffic that triggered prewarm logic and caused epoch snapshot conflicts during a brief scheduler reconfiguration.

Expected behavior:
- Explicit tenant pin should be preserved and honored even during simultaneous shadow-replay/scale events; orchestrator should queue pin deltas without dropping or reverting to fallback for committed sessions.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Grafana: dashboards/routing/pin-reconciliation (spike at 2026-03-14T09:08Z)
- Sentry events: SVC-FALLBACK-INVOCATION id=svc-61820 (see linked PR for probe)
- Edge logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/carousel/2026-03-14/edge-logs-09-08.gz (filtered keys attached to customer ticket)

Initial investigation notes:
- Observation shows orchestrator applied a snapshot that did not include the most recent tenant pin delta for ~2 internal epochs. Hypothesis: snapshot merge backoff + shadow-replay prewarm produced an ordering where the pin delta was persisted to only a subset of meta-shards before the routing snapshot was promoted.
- Edge proxy header sanitizer ran concurrently and rewrote a keepalive header in a small % of requests; those requests lost the x-tenant-pin attribute and hit the fallback routing.
- Autoscaler prewarm caused extra warm-up allocations and increased snapshot churn.

Temporary mitigations executed:
- Support temporarily disabled the shadow-replay job for rw-g1-large-v2 for the dedicated pool (09:25 UTC) which halted new overlay prewarm traffic.
- Applied manual pin reassertion for affected tenant cohorts via orchestration admin tool at 09:31 UTC.
- Added a short-term routing rule to prefer pin-coherent shards for Carousel Labs until reconciliation completes.

Current status / next steps:
1) Engineering (orchestrator + routing) to reproduce ordering locally using replay harness (assigned Diego).
2) Add stronger write-ahead commit gating to snapshot promotion to ensure pin deltas are included atomically or withheld until consistent across shards.
3) Edge: investigate header sanitizer ordering with proxy keepalive codepath and harden x-tenant-pin preservation in the sanitizer.
4) Add tracer tags for pin-delta origin and snapshot-epoch in routing logs for easier root-cause duration queries.
5) Post-incident: discuss whether shadow-replay should be automatically throttled when tenant dedicated pools are under prewarm/autoscale pressure.

Customer communications:
- CS notified customer at 09:40 UTC with temporary workaround and ETA for fix.
- Promise: follow-up with timeline and postmortem within 48 hours.
comments: 2026-03-14 09:18 - Maya Patel (Support): Customer reported mixed outputs. Captured sample session IDs and slices. Escalating to SRE; tagging Diego.
2026-03-14 09:27 - Diego Ramirez (SRE): Got heap of edge logs. Shadow-replay job active at time of surge. Paused shadow job and reasserted pins. Noted pin_reconcile_latency spike in Grafana.
2026-03-14 09:35 - Support (Maya): Customer acknowledged temporary mitigation but still seeing occasional degraded responses (approx 2% of requests). Collecting more traces per Diego's request.

2026-03-14 10:02 - Diego Ramirez (SRE): Confirmed header sanitizer mutated keepalive header on ~1.8% of proxied requests for that shard. Creating a fix PR to preserve x-tenant-pin ahead of sanitizer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/903

2026-03-14 10:30 - Product (Anika Shah): Noted this intersects with our canary policy: recommend adding a guard to prevent shadow-replay from triggering prewarm in dedicated pools. Added to backlog and creating linked internal ticket INT-8142.
2026-03-14 11:05 - Support (Maya) to Customer: We pushed a temporary routing rule and paused the replay. We're continuing root cause analysis and will share a timeline for a permanent fix.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations: shadow-replay paused, manual reassertion of pins, short-term routing rule. Engineering will implement snapshot promotion gating and proxy sanitizer fix. Follow-up: postmortem and automatic shadow-replay throttling when dedicated pools are prewarming.
